chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The menstruating woman recites the Quran, and the post-childbirth bleeding woman, and the one in major ritual impurity as well.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman recite the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition on reciting the Quran applies specifically to the physical act of touching the mus'haf (copy of the Quran) or the state of minor impurity (hadath) for some scholars, rather than an absolute ban on vocal recitation for women in major impurity states (junub, hayd, nufas). It reflects the Shia juristic view that menstruating and post-childbirth women may recite verses directly from memory or from the book, distinguishing this from the strict prohibition on non-pure individuals entering the Masjid al-Haram. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity and Quranic engagement during daily life.
